title: Luke Bible Quiz - Chapter 21
description: Ten questions on Luke 21: the poor widow's gift, the words about the temple, the signs and troubles to come, the fig tree and the nights on Olivet.

questions.text: What did the poor widow cast into the treasury?
questions.explanation: He saw a certain poor widow casting in two small brass coins.

answers.text: A small gold ring
Two small brass coins
A jar of olive oil
A measure of grain

questions.text: Why did he say the widow had put in more than all the others?
questions.explanation: The others gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in all that she had to live on.

answers.text: She gave the same amount every day
She had promised her gift beforehand
She gave in secret while the others looked on
She put in all that she had to live on

questions.text: What did he say would happen to the temple stones people were admiring?
questions.explanation: He said that of the things they saw, there would not be left one stone on another that would not be thrown down.

answers.text: Not one stone would be left on another
They would be carried away to another land
They would shine brighter than before
They would be covered with gold

questions.text: What did he warn that many would say when they came in his name?
questions.explanation: He warned them not to be led astray, for many would come in his name saying, "I am he," and, "The time is at hand."

answers.text: "The temple will stand forever"
"Peace is upon this city"
"I am he" and "The time is at hand"
"Follow Moses and the prophets"

questions.text: What did he say there would be in various places?
questions.explanation: He said there would be great earthquakes, famines, and plagues in various places, and terrors and great signs from heaven.

answers.text: Floods and heavy hailstorms
Great earthquakes, famines, and plagues
New temples and new altars
Long years of peace and plenty

questions.text: Why did he tell them not to prepare beforehand how to answer?
questions.explanation: He told them to settle it in their hearts not to plan their answer in advance, because he would give them a mouth and wisdom that their adversaries could not withstand or contradict.

answers.text: An angel from heaven would speak the words for them
The judges would release them without any trial
He would give them a mouth and wisdom their adversaries could not withstand
Their parents and relatives would defend them

questions.text: What sign did he give that Jerusalem's desolation was at hand?
questions.explanation: He said that when they see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then they should know that its desolation is at hand.

answers.text: Seeing the temple gates shut at noon
Hearing of a famine in Judea
Seeing a star stand over the city
Seeing Jerusalem surrounded by armies

questions.text: How did he say the Son of Man would be seen coming?
questions.explanation: He said they would see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

answers.text: In a cloud with power and great glory
Riding on a horse through the city gate
Walking quietly among the crowds
Standing in the temple at midnight

questions.text: In the parable of the trees, what does their budding tell you?
questions.explanation: He said that when the fig tree and all the trees are already budding, you see it and know by yourselves that the summer is already near.

answers.text: That the harvest has been lost
That the rains are over for good
That the summer is already near
That a storm is coming

questions.text: Where did Jesus spend his nights while he taught in the temple each day?
questions.explanation: Every day he was teaching in the temple, and every night he would go out and spend the night on the mountain that is called Olivet.

answers.text: In the house of the high priest
On the mountain called Olivet
In the temple courtyard
In a village across the Jordan
